text:
taylor_sales: Heads-up — new enterprise POC incoming from AstroHealth. They want Redwood to run their MarinerX-70B-finetuned model. Key asks: safetensors HF repo, 32k+ KV cache, int8 quant, private VPC deployment, p95 SLA ~50ms for chat. Also sent a security questionnaire that asks about KMS/HSM and data residency. Can SE/infra advise on compatibility, perf blockers, and a pricing ballpark? cc @nora_se @deepak_infra

nora_se: quick questions — does the HF repo include tokenizer.json and model config? any custom attention/rope implementation? Those affect kernel selection. Also for int8 we need to know whether they expect q4f/q5 or some custom quant. If you can drop repo link and a small sample of prompts that'd help.

deepak_infra: VPC/private deploy is supported. KV cache >32k is doable but expensive — need to estimate KV memory. Also for 70B + 32k context we'll likely need dedicated nodes or KV offload. For SLA 50ms p95 we should validate what they mean (per-token vs end-to-end). We'll need QPS and prompt length distribution.

sara_prod: For catalog fit: if model is standard HF safetensors/tokenizer we can onboard as a variant. If tokenizer differs we may need an adapter layer. Suggest checklist: 1) HF repo link + safely sharable weights; 2) tokenizer and config; 3) 100 sample prompts with expected outputs; 4) security questionnaire; 5) expected QPS/peak. I'll prepare the checklist.

taylor_sales: repo: https://huggingface.co/astrohealth/marinerx-70b-ft v1 — includes safetensors and tokenizer.json. Attaching small sample prompt set. They asked: do we need to recompile/convert for int8 or can you do it in-place? Also what's a ballpark per-token cost for 70B int8 hosted vs dedicated?

nora_se: We usually run conversion through our quant pipeline. Example convert command we use internally: 
```
redwood-quantize --input marinerx.safetensors --method q4f --out marinerx-int8.pt
```
After conversion we validate numerics and run a perf harness. Very rough hosted per-token estimate for 70B int8: $0.30–$0.50 per 1k tokens (depends on batching/KV hit rate). Dedicated reserved capacity will be lower — depends on commit. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

deepak_infra: rough KV memory calc: 70B model with 32k context ≈ 420GB of KV (very rough ballpark). With int8+sharding and KV compression/offload we can fit across 6–8 x 80GB GPUs in Dedicated, or use KV offload on disk but that kills latency. For on-prem they'll need rack-level GPU capacity. So answer: possible, but expect infra procurement and higher cost.

taylor_sales: noted. I'll ask them for QPS and max prompt lengths. Who will run the perf sweep once they give artifacts?

sara_prod: I can coordinate the smoke tests on hosted first, then we'll move to Dedicated perf runs. Important: clarify SLA language — 50ms p95 for 32k context + 70B is unrealistic without heavy engineering/fallback. Recommend a canary route with fallback to smaller variant (e.g., MarinerX-13B) for tail latency.

nora_se: :thumbsup: I'll queue a perf run once their artifacts arrive. Also please have them sign the model license attestation if the weights aren't public.

taylor_sales: I'll own the security questionnaire replies and license attestation. I'll loop in @jordan_compliance if they push HSM/KMS specifics. Thanks everyone — I'll update when I get QPS and the full SQ back.
